TL;DR: On drivers after 591.74, while a display calibration (gamma ramp / video LUT) is loaded, black and near-black are shown 1-2 levels too bright. This lasts as long as the calibration is loaded. With no calibration loaded, nothing is wrong. 591.74 is correct in every case.

* GPU: GeForce RTX 3060 Ti

* CPU: Intel Core i7-10700KF

* Display Configuration: Dell U2419H (DisplayPort) and Acer S240HL (HDMI). 8 bpc RGB, Output dynamic range set to Full.

* Operating System: Windows 11 Home, build 26200

* Driver Regression: Yes. Last good driver: 591.74. Bad: 621.14 (full A/B test below); also seen on 610.88 and 621.01. Not tested: 591.86, 596.21, 596.36, 610.47. All Game Ready drivers, standard package.

A/B test on the same day, same display, same calibration file and same steps (X-Rite i1 Display Pro colorimeter, ArgyllCMS, calibration loader closed). Black in cd/m2, white about 86 cd/m2.

- Calibrated contrast report (dispcal -R): Driver 591.74 = 973:1. Driver 621.14 = 746:1.
- Switching from my calibration back to a linear ramp: Driver 591.74 = black correct immediately. Driver 621.14 = black one level too high (0.116) for about 25 seconds, then correct.
- No calibration loaded (dispcal -r, 3 runs): Driver 591.74 = 973:1. Driver 621.14 = 972-974:1. No difference.

- In the 25 seconds after a switch, levels 8, 16, 250 and 254 are also one level too high. Levels 32 to 230 and white are not affected.

Hi everyone,

I’m experiencing recurring freezes followed by automatic restarts on my PC while watching videos or live streams in Google Chrome. This has happened several times, including twice on the same day. The entire PC freezes and then restarts without any manual intervention.

**System specifications:**

- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D.
- **Motherboard:** ASUS TUF GAMING B850-PLUS WIFI.
- **BIOS:** 1681.
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, 16 GB GDDR7.
- **Power supply:** Corsair RM1000x SHIFT, 1000 W.
- **Current NVIDIA driver:** 621.14, confirmed using `nvidia-smi`.

**Symptoms and troubleshooting so far:**

- The issue occurred with driver **617.42** and has continued with **621.14**.
- I performed a clean driver installation using the NVIDIA installer, but **I have not used DDU yet**.
- Chrome’s “Use graphics acceleration when available” setting is currently disabled. I cannot confirm whether it was disabled before all the previous crashes.
**Crash dump findings:**
The dumps analyzed so far indicate **VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0x116)**, involving **nvlddmkm.sys**. I understand that this identifies a failure in the graphics timeout recovery process but does not, by itself, establish whether the underlying cause is the driver or hardware.
Has anyone experienced similar restarts during video playback with an RTX 5080 and these driver versions? Would a cleanup with DDU be a reasonable next step, and what additional logs or tests would help distinguish a driver issue from a GPU, power supply, or other hardware problem?

Title: NVIDIA Driver Regression – G-SYNC Stuttering with Multiple Windows Open

System: Windows 11, Gigabyte RTX 4090 Gaming OC, Intel i7-13700KF, dual ASUS ROG Swift OLED PG32UCWM monitors (4K 240 Hz, DisplayPort). NVIDIA driver version: 621.14

Issue: Following a recent NVIDIA driver update, Oxygen Not Included (ONI) experiences severe intermittent stuttering when another application is open on the secondary monitor. During WASD camera movement, the game periodically freezes or hitches before suddenly catching up. The issue occurs with unrelated applications, including Chrome (even with an empty tab) and Windows Photos.

Reproduction: Enable G-SYNC, launch ONI on the primary monitor, open Chrome or Windows Photos on the secondary monitor, and continuously scroll the game camera using WASD. Closing the secondary application immediately eliminates the stuttering.
Troubleshooting: Disabling G-SYNC completely resolves the issue. Disabling Chrome hardware acceleration has no effect. Disabling Windows Multi-Plane Overlay (MPO) and restarting also has no effect. Verifying game files and reverting from the ONI beta to the stable version did not resolve it.
Suspected Cause: The issue appears to be an NVIDIA driver issue involving G-SYNC frame presentation when multiple application windows are open. The problem began following a driver update and is reproducible across unrelated secondary applications.
Please investigate this potential driver regression affecting multi-monitor G-SYNC configurations.

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER (VBIOS 95.04.69.00.c1, PCIe 4.0 x16)

CPU: Intel Core i5-14600KF (14C/20T)

Display Configuration: 1x LG UltraGear, connected via DisplayPort, 1920x1080 @ 144 Hz (single display)

Operating System: Windows 11 Home 25H2 (build 26200.9711)

Driver Regression: Yes, new in 621.14. Driver 621.01 (clean install) is NOT affected: nvlog.nvlgstg grows ~0.5 KB/min and NVDisplay.Container.exe writes < 2 MB per 5 min, vs ~325 KB/min growth and 515 MB per 5 min on 621.14 under the same conditions.

Affected Applications/Games: None specific. It happens at the desktop with no games running (only a web browser with 2 tabs open). It is not tied to any game.

Issue Description:
NVDisplay.Container.exe (service "NVIDIA Display Container LS") continuously rewrites the binary log file
C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg, causing heavy SSD writes while the PC is idle.
- Resource Monitor showed NVDisplay.Container.exe writing 4.6–5.2 MB/s to this file, with no game running.
- The file grows quickly after being cleared (0 → 2.6 MB in about 8 minutes) and reached about 20 MB. The write volume increases as the file grows.
- Over a 5-minute idle measurement, NVDisplay.Container.exe accounted for 515 MB of write I/O. After stopping the service, deleting nvlog.nvlgstg and restarting the service, it dropped to 48 MB (-91%), and total writes to the C: drive dropped from 270 MB to 145 MB.
- The SSD's SMART "Data Units Written" counter matches the writes Windows reports, so these are real writes to the NVMe drive.
This causes unnecessary SSD wear (about 3 GB/hour from this process alone at idle). A similar issue with nvtopps.db3 was fixed in driver 471.96 in 2021.
1. Install driver 621.14 with the NVIDIA App (default settings; no NVIDIA Control Panel changes).
3. Open Resource Monitor > Disk and sort by Write (B/s): NVDisplay.Container.exe keeps writing several MB/s to C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\...
4. Check C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg: it is modified every few seconds and keeps growing.
5. Workaround that confirms the source: stop the "NVIDIA Display Container LS" service, delete nvlog.nvlgstg, and restart the service. Writes drop by about 91% until the file grows again.
